definition: The practice of taking a model trained on one task or dataset and adapting it to a different but related task, leveraging previously learned representations.
details: Transfer learning underlies the modern pretrain-then-fine-tune paradigm, allowing models to reuse general knowledge learned from large datasets rather than learning every task from scratch.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. Think of it this way: The practice of taking a model trained on one task or dataset and adapting it to a different but related task, leveraging previously learned representations. And here is the clever part: Transfer learning underlies the modern pretrain-then-fine-tune paradigm, allowing models to reuse general knowledge learned from large datasets rather than learning every task from scratch. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. And that is Transfer Learning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
